title: One Task, One Timer.
body:
Many years ago, when I was studying and writing assignments, I followed the idea of focusing on one task at a time. I expanded this approach by adding a timer to each task, and I found it extremely helpful.

After completing my degree, I gradually drifted away from this method.

More recently, as my life circumstances have changed, I’ve found it harder to concentrate. So I’ve returned to the principle of focusing on a single activity at a time—no multitasking. I’ve also found that this works best when the activity is planned for a limited, defined period. This allows for regular breaks, which helps prevent mental fatigue and overload, and it adds a helpful sense of structure.

You can extend these timed periods if you wish, as long as you include breaks. I use this app to manage that.

If you want to maximise your results and be as productive as possible, I recommend using the Pomodoro timer and technique alongside your daily plan. It helps maintain structure and keeps you focused on each task.

It will improve the quality of your life.

title: Does what it says on the tin
body:
This app provides a full-screen timer, nicely laid out, showing numerical countdown as well as a simulated rotary timer. The app is extremely focussed on helping you use the Pomodoro Technique. Go read up about it on Wikipedia if you haven't heard of this popular productivity tool.

The timer has three "phases": the work, rest and long-break phases. The default configuration is four "pomodoros" of 25 minutes broken by a 5 minute rest, with a 25 minute long break at the end. You can manually adjust the timers, though setting default durations for each period is only possible in the paid app.

The ticking sound is a nice reminder that you are supposed to be focussed on one task. Some people won't like it, you can turn it off in the paid version of the app.

The app also includes daily goals of 12 pomodoros. Achievement of this goal is reported through charts.

My only quibble with this app was the end of period alerts which are once-off chimes. They are easy to miss when listening to music. You do get banner notifications though.

For many people, using the Clock app on your iPad or iPhone will work just as well, though I find this app is more charming than Apple's timer app. The charm keeps me using this Pomodoro timer though!
